senses.gloss:
लुभ् लुभ्, cl. 4. P. लुभ्यति, लुलोभ
(A. लुलुभे), लोभिष्यति, अलुभत्, लो-
भितुम्, लोब्धुम्, to desire greatly or eagerly,
covet, long for anything (dat. or loc.); to be inter-
ested in; to allure, (मां लुलुभे, he allured me);
to be perplexed or disturbed, become disordered, go
astray; cl. 6. P. लुभति, &c., Aor. अलोभीत्, to be-
wilder, confound, perplex, disturb: Caus. लोभयति,
&c., to cause to desire or long for, make greedy; ex-
cite greediness or covetousness, excite lust; to allure,
entice, entice away, seduce, attract; to disturb, de-
range: Desid. लुलुभिषति, लुलोभिषति: Intens.
लोलुभ्यते, लोलोब्धि; [cf. Gr. λίψ, λιψ-ουρία,
λίπ-τ-ομαι, ἐλευθερός: Lat. lub-et, lib-et, lib-ī-do,
lib-er, Libentina: Goth. liub-s, ‘dear;’ brothra-
lub-o, us-laubjan: Old Germ. liub-an, môt-luba,
lob, lob-ô-n: Angl. Sax. leof, lyfan, lufian, lof,
leaf, left: Slav. ljub-i-ti, ‘to love;’ liub-y, ljub-
imi, liub-y-ti, liub-jaus: Lith. lubju.]

लुभित, अस्, आ, अम्, perplexed, disturbed, de-
luded, fascinated.
लुभित्वा, ind. having perplexed or disturbed, &c.

लुभ्यत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, desiring greatly, coveting,
longing for.
